title: Adaptive AI and quantum computing for real-time financial fraud detection and cyber-attack prevention in U.S. healthcare
journal_or_venue: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews
abstract_summary: The paper proposes a hybrid framework that integrates adaptive AI (deep neural networks and reinforcement learning) with quantum computing techniques (quantum annealing and quantum machine learning) to enable real-time financial fraud detection and cyber-attack prevention in the U.S. healthcare sector. Empirical case studies and evaluations report improved detection accuracy over traditional methods, and the authors discuss ethical, privacy, and regulatory implications for responsible deployment.
methodology_description: The study proposes a hybrid framework that integrates adaptive AI and quantum computing for real-time financial fraud detection and cyber-attack prevention in U.S. healthcare. Methodologically, the framework is structured into three main components: (1) data preprocessing (data cleaning, feature extraction, normalization), (2) adaptive AI modeling (deep neural networks for non-linear pattern learning, reinforcement learning using Q-learning for continuous adaptation, and federated learning via federated averaging for privacy-preserving multi-party training), and (3) quantum-enhanced optimization (quantum annealing to search for global minima of model loss functions and a quantum support vector machine (QSVM) for anomaly/classification tasks). Data integration steps (aggregation, transformation, validation) are performed to combine sources from HHS, CISA, NIST and multiple providers. Performance is evaluated with standard classification metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1) and statistical hypothesis testing (paired t-test) to compare the hybrid approach against classical baselines. Case studies are cited (e.g., analyses of >1M claims) to illustrate empirical improvements, but the paper does not report low-level implementation details such as quantum hardware configuration, specific software frameworks, or hyperparameter settings.

results_summary: The paper proposes a hybrid framework combining adaptive AI (deep neural networks, reinforcement learning, federated learning) with quantum-enhanced optimization (quantum annealing and QSVM) for real-time fraud detection and cyber-attack prevention in U.S. healthcare. It reports case-study level improvements over classical methods—most prominently a reported increase in fraud detection accuracy from 85% to 95%—and improvements across precision, recall and F1 metrics, with a paired t-test yielding p < 0.001. The work also highlights privacy-preserving federated approaches and quantum cryptography (QKD and lattice-based schemes) as safeguards. The claimed quantum computational advantages (e.g., exponential speedups) are presented theoretically and via limited case-study results; broad, production-scale quantum advantage is not demonstrated and remains speculative. The paper also contains a notable error in the stated recall formula that contradicts standard definitions.
